{{quote|The Sith species eventually vanished, but the legacy of their language remained not only with planets that they touched, but also with the members of various other species, including humans, who sought the Force heritage the Sith left behind. As a result, the Sith language long outlasted the Sith species, both as an arcane language of dark side devotees and a lingering legacy of ancient conquests amongst other peoples.|Dr. [[Milanda Vorgan]], "[[The Written Word: A Brief Introduction to the Writing Systems of Galactic Basic]]''|<ref name="TWW" />}}
'''Sith''' was the native language of [[Sith (species)/Legends|the people]] of [[Ziost/Legends|Ziost]] and [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]]. It was adopted as the mystical language of the [[Sith/Legends|Sith Order]] after the [[Exiles|Dark Jedi Exiles]] enslaved the Sith species. Sith was an agglutinative language, in which words or even phrases were made up of linears sequences of distinct meaningful units. Despite the preeminence of the [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]], the Sith language remained in use up until the [[Post-Imperial era/Legends|post-Imperial era]]. To the [[Lost Tribe of Sith]], an order founded on the remote [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kesh/Legends|Kesh]], the Sith language was known as '''the Old Tongue'''.

==Usage==
{{Quote|Dzworokka yun; nyâshqûwai, nwiqûwai. Wotok tsawakmidwanottoi, yuntok hyarutmidwanottoi|The Rule of Two|<ref name="SLS" />}}
Originally, this language was only spoken by the [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith]], a [[Species/Legends|species]] of [[Color/Legends|red]]&ndash;skinned [[Humanoid/Legends|Humanoids]]<ref name="JvS">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref> from the [[Stygian Caldera]].<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> It was later expanded upon and evolved when the second generation of [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Hundred-Year Darkness/Legends|split]] from the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] in [[7000 BBY]], just after the [[Battle of Corbos]], and enslaved the natives of [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]].<ref name="JvS" /> The Sith language became a symbol of the newly created [[Sith/Legends|Sith Order]], a powerful sect of [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] adepts. This was made easier through the creation of devices known as [[Translation Talisman/Legends|translation talismans]].<ref name="TOTJIni" /> Such artifacts, initially designed and created by the Jedi Exiles who sought to learn of the Sith's secrets, allowed their wearer to read the Sith language as if it were their own mother tongue.<ref name="TOJC">''[[Tales of the Jedi Companion]]''</ref> The [[Code of the Sith/Legends|Code of the Sith]], originally penned in Basic by the Exile [[Sorzus Syn]] and inspired by the lifestyle of the Sith Purebloods,<ref name="TBoS" /> was also translated in Sith language as Qotsisajak.<ref name="Grossblatt e-mail2">{{EmailCite|email=Wookieepedia:Email/Ben Grossblatt (2013)|creator=[[Ben Grossblatt]]|date=2012-07-25}}</ref>

Around [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], the [[Sith dreadnaught]] ''[[Omen]]'' was forced to crash land on the remote [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kesh/Legends|Kesh]]. The marrooned Sith were never able to to return to space, so they settled amongst the native [[Keshiri/Legends|Keshiri]] and founded the [[Lost Tribe of Sith]]. This allowed the Sith language to expand far from its cradle.<ref name="LotSPr" /> In this marginal Sith colony, the language became known as "the Old Tongue".<ref name="Ascension">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Ascension]]''</ref>

[[File:Atrissholocron.jpg|thumb|Three of Master Atris's Sith holocrons]]
Even after the majority of Sith were of other species than the Sith Pureblood, the language was preserved in [[Holocron/Legends|holocrons]],<ref name="K2">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref> temples, and tomes.<ref name="TOTJIni" /> However, outside of the dark side circles, very few scholars knew how to decipher this language, and even fewer could pronounce its complex word structures.<ref name="TOJC" /> Much later, in the eleventh century before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]] became familiar with the tongue of the ancient Sith during his studies at the [[Sith Academy (Korriban)|Academy]] of Korriban, unlike most of his fellow students. Bane would seek the wisdom of Masters long [[Death/Legends|dead]] in [[Leather/Legends|leather]]-bound volumes covered with [[Blood/Legends|blood]]-red ink.<ref name="DBRT" />

Millennia after the founding of the Sith Order, individuals as modern as the fallen Jedi [[Vergere]]<ref name="VMM">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20021219vergere|text=Vergere, Master of Mystery}}</ref> and [[Jerec (Inquisitor)|Jerec]]<ref name="The Dark Forces Saga Part 6">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20050616a|series=The Dark Forces Saga|text=Part 6: Outcasts and Megalomaniacs Welcome}}</ref> or the [[Sullustan/Legends|Sullustan]] [[Naturalist/Legends|naturalist]] [[Dr'uun Unnh/Legends|Dr'uun Unnh]],<ref name="I, Jedi">''[[I, Jedi]]''</ref> spoke it. The members of the Lost Tribe of Sith also managed to preserve the knowledge of the Old Tongue, and all members from apprentices and higher knew it. For example, [[Vestara Khai]] was able to use it to communicate with a pack of [[Tuk'ata/Legends|Tuk'ata]] on Korriban.<ref name="Ascension" /> The last members of the [[Order of the Sith Lords]] founded by Bane, [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] and his successive apprentices [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]], [[Dooku/Legends|Darth Tyranus]] and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], were all capable of speaking Sith fluently.<ref name="DSS">''[[The Dark Side Sourcebook]]''</ref>

==Phonology and accent==
The phonetic palette of the Sith language consisted of 23 phonemes or speech sounds. There were approximately 11 obstruents and 6 or 7 sonorants: /t/, /d/, /k/, /q/, /m/, /n/, /ts/, /dz/, /s/, /z/, /h/, /t͡ʃ/,/j/ /ʃ/, [ɹ/l], /w/, /ʎ/ . Accordingly, the graphemic system to represent these was ''t'', ''d'', ''k'', ''q'', ''m'', ''n'', ''ts'', ''dz'', ''s'', ''z'', ''h'', ''ch'', ''j'', ''sh'', ''r/l'', ''w'', ''y''.<ref name="SLS" />

There were also 6 distinct vowels: /i/ or ''i'' (as in "heat"), /æ/ or ''â'' (as in "bash"), /u/ or ''u'' (as in "suit"), /ʌ/ or ''û'' (as in "club"), /oʊ/ or ''o'' (as in "toad"), /ɑ/ or ''a'' (as in "ah"). In addition, ''a'' and ''o'' would combine with ''i'' to make diphthongs: ''oi'' (as in "toy") and ''ai'' (as in "buy"). The epenthetic vowel was /u/.<ref name="SLS" />

Because of this limited segment inventory, Sith scribes faced difficulties when trying to translate non-Sith names. For example, the name of [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] would have to be transcribed as ''Marmûtin'', as the Sith language did not have a "p" sound or an "l" between two consonants. To overcome such difficulties, creative scribes would actually translate the name into their language based on its etymology. Assimilation from borrowed lexical items is preferred by place of articulation: in Palpatine, /p/ > /m/.<ref name="SLS" />

Sith morphemes&mdash;the smallest meaningful units in the grammar of a language&mdash;were often made of closed syllables (syllables ending with consonants), which made them sound brisk and choppy. The language was regularly stressed, with every word accented on the first syllable.<ref name="SLS" />

The Sith language discouraged vowels in hiatus, and glides /j/ or /ʎ/ were inserted when two vowels appeared next to each other. The phrase ''siqsayanjat'' ("about a demon") was in fact composed of ''siqsa'' ("demon") and ''anjat'' (ablative noun marker), with the addition of the glide ''y'' to eliminate the hiatus.<ref name="Grossblatt e-mail">{{EmailCite|email=Wookieepedia:Email/Ben Grossblatt|creator=[[Ben Grossblatt]]|date=2012-07-16}}</ref>

==Morphology==
The language of the Sith extensively employed regular agglutination and used derivative suffixes to a greater extent than [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]]. Many different markers could be added to a root until very long words were formed&mdash;and a single word could constitute an entire sentence. For example, the phrase "because of dreaming about a demon" translated in Sith as a single word ''kûskutsiqsayanjat''. This word was made of four distinct morphemes: ''kûsk'' + ''ut'' + ''siqsa'' + ''(y)anjat'' = "to dream" + (nominal verb marker) + "demon" + (ablative noun marker). Some markers could be added only to nouns, and others only to verbs.<ref name="SLS" />

==Grammar==
===Word order===
The typical declarative word order of Sith was verb / subject / object &mdash; for example, "Wonoksh Qyâsik nun" was literally "Shall free / the Force / me". However, there also existed prepositional phrases, and subjects or objects could sometimes be put at the front of the sentence for emphasis.<ref name="Grossblatt e-mail2" />

===Verbs===
Verb roots were typically one syllable and ended with a consonant. Moods, tenses, and other subtleties were indicated by suffixation verb markers. For example, the addition of ''-atul'' expressed the alethic mood, the speaker's belief that an action was logically necessary or obviously true. (The phrase ''Châts nu midwan'' would be "I gain power", while its alethic form ''Châtsatul nu midwan'' could be translated as "I necessarily gain power.") Also, the addition of ''-oksh'' expressed future tense. (For instance, ''Won Qyâsik nun'' meant "The Force frees me," while ''Wonoksh Qyâsik nun'' meant "The Force shall free me.") The suffix ''-win'' was sometimes added to a transitive verb to indicate ergativity, meaning that the grammatical subject of that verb was in fact its semantic object, while the true semantic agent remained unexpressed. (In the phrase ''kotswinot itsu'' or "my chains break," the action described is in fact being done to the subject ''itsu'' by an undetermined agent.)<ref name="Grossblatt e-mail2" /> Thanks to the suffix ''-ut'', verbs could also be nominalized. (For example, ''kûsk'' was "to dream" while ''kûskut'' was "the act of dreaming.")<ref name="SLS" />

===Nouns===
Sith nouns had cases, inflectional forms indicating their grammatical relation to other words in the sentence. Those cases were expressed by the addition of a noun marker. Known cases were the instrumental case (''-jontû''), the ablative case (''-anjat''), the dative case (''-ottoi''). Instrumental case indicated that the noun it marked was the means of the accomplishment of the action expressed by the clause; for instance, ''ashajontû'' meant "through victory." As regards the ablative case, it could be best translated in Basic using the preposition "about." The word ''siqsayanjat'' meant "about/concerning a demon." A noun was in the dative case when it was used as an indirect object: ''midwan'' was "power" while ''midwanottoi'' meant "for/to the power."<ref name="SLS" />

==Written forms==
{{Quote|By the Empress! I... I can read it perfectly!''"<br />"''Of course you can, my son.|[[Satal Keto/Legends|Satal Keto]] acquiring the knowledge of Sith language from [[King/Legends|King]] [[Ommin/Legends|Ommin]]|<ref name="TOTJIni">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Freedon Nadd Uprising 2|''Tales of the Jedi – The Freedon Nadd Uprising'' 2]]</ref>}}
[[File:Exar_Kun_reading_Sith.png|thumb|left|Exar Kun reading Sith hieroglyphs]]
The Sith language was originally written in complex hieroglyphics. Over the [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]], Sith scribes wished to develop less complicated scripts. This resulted in the creation of two different scripts. The first one, known as "[[Common Sith]]" was used for mundane, everyday use, while the other, "[[High Sith]]" was for ecclesiastical use.<ref name="TWW" /> A third writing system known as the [[Kittât]] was also used for incantation scrolls. The latter consisted of thirty-seven runes, and was suitable for both calligraphy and epigraphy.<ref name="SLS" />
[[File:HighSithWriting.jpg|thumb|The spellbook of Freedon Nadd was written in Sith]]
The [[Massassi/Legends|Massassi]] warriors who followed the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Naga Sadow/Legends|Naga Sadow]] in [[Exile (punishment)/Legends|exile]] on the [[Yavin 4/Legends|fourth]] [[Moon/Legends|moon]] of [[Yavin Prime/Legends|Yavin Prime]] also developed their own hieroglyphic system, a simplified version of High Sith. They carved many inscriptions using this [[Massassi (alphabet)|new writing system]] on [[Massassi Temple|temple]] walls and obelisks scattered across the jungle of Yavin 4,<ref name="TWW" /> notably in the [[Temple of the Blueleaf Cluster/Legends|Temple of the Blueleaf Cluster]]<ref name="I, Jedi" /> or at the monumental rear entrance of the [[Great Temple/Legends|Great Temple]].<ref name="ISWU">''[[The Illustrated Star Wars Universe]]''</ref> When the [[Sullustan/Legends|Sullustan]] naturalist Dr'uun Unnh explored Yavin 4 on behalf of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]], he successfully translated some of the Massassi texts contained in the [[Temple of Exar Kun]].<ref name="ISWU" /> When the [[New Jedi Order]] of [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] established its [[Jedi Praxeum|academy]] on Yavin 4, Skywalker and some of his students learnt to decipher that script, which allowed them to read the [[Books of Massassi]].<ref name="BtS">''[[Before the Storm]]''</ref>

==Known phrases==
*''Dzworokka yun; nyâshqûwai, nwiqûwai. Wotok tsawakmidwanottoi, yuntok hyarutmidwanottoi.''&mdash;"Two there should be; no more, no less. One to embody power, the other to crave it."<ref name="SLS" />
*''Eyah seh maat, shu kor huaan.''&mdash;Unknown. Something soothing.<ref name="Ascension" />
*''Haa, neyo la yud masur kee, tah uhnah kahru lur shu.''&mdash;Unknown. Something menacing and challenging.<ref name="Ascension" />
*''Ja'ak.''&mdash;"I am free."<ref name="KPLS">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20031002korriban1|series=Korriban: Planet of Lost Souls|text=Part 1: Haunted Hideout}}</ref>
*''Na-hah ur su ka-haat. Su ka haru aat.''&mdash;Unknown. Most likely something as: "Lead the Sith to us if there are any here."<ref name="Ascension" />
*''Taka zeech ma toka duuwaj.''&mdash;Unknown. An incantation to gain access to a Sith obelisk.<ref name="TOJC" />
*''Ur-kaa!''&mdash;Unknown. Probably something such as "Halt!" or "Freeze!"<ref name="Ascension" />
*''Vexok savaka.''&mdash;"Wake up, there is work to do."<ref name="KPLS" />
*''Zhol kash dinora.''&mdash;"It is done."<ref name="KPLS" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|To that end, I imagined a tough&mdash;but not barbarous&mdash;language, one that could convey a kind of confident, elegant cruelty. And Sith would have to ring with authority so you could envision it functioning among elites of the dark side the way Latin functioned in Europe for centuries: as a repository of culture and learning.|Ben Grossblatt|<ref name="SLS" />}}
[[File:Unpronounceable_Sith.png|thumb|200px|Early incarnation of the Sith language]]
The Sith language first appeared in the 1990s [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] series [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi (comic series)|''Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi'']]. At the time, occurrences of that language consisted of nonsensical words, composed only of unpronounceable series of consonants&mdash;such as ''Nkrttw flgkllm shprrlt mdnnq''.<ref name="TOJDDJ" /> This version of Sith does not blend well with ulterior appearances in canon, and should probably be considered an artistic license. In ''Speak Like a Sith'', Ben Grossblatt noted that no one would even try to speak a language if it consisted of unpronounceable words like ''r'rhhoqtk''.<ref name="SLS" /> However, in the [[Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith (audio drama)|audio drama adaptation]] of ''Tales of the Jedi'', the instances were Exar Kun speaks Sith sounded very different from their comic book counterpart, featuring a variety of vocalic sounds.<ref name="TOJAD">[[Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith (audio drama)|''Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith'' audio drama]]</ref>

In the [[2004]] video game ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]'', Darth Nihilus was heard communicating in the same fashion as the Sith holocrons kept by Atris, leading some fans to believe that the Dark Lord spoke Sith. However, when working on the ''[[Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide]]'', ''Star Wars'' author [[Abel G. Peña]] wrote a whole passage devoted to [[Mask of Darth Nihilus|Nihilus' mask]] that was ultimately cut. It would have notably provided two scholarly explanations of Nihilus' speech. According to that cut passage, the Dark Lord's hissings may have either been the last language ever spoken in the galaxy, billions of years into the future, at the end of time, or the raw dialect of the Force itself, untranslated by [[Midi-chlorian/Legends|midi-chlorians]].<ref name="tfn">{{JCFCite|url=posts/50677352|board=Literature|thread=Obscure Droids and Ewoks comics -- translated by Abel Peña|user=[[Abel G. Peña|Halagad_Ventor]]|date=2013-04-27|time=01:11 AM|archivedate=20171105191827}}</ref>

[[File:Speak_like_a_Sith.jpg|thumb|left|200px|''Speak Like a Sith'']]
In [[November]] [[2010]], senior editor [[Ben Grossblatt]], who has degrees in linguistics, created a functional Sith language for the ''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''. His work included Sith rules of grammar and sentence construction and a Sith runic script. More information about the creation of this language was revealed in ''[[Speak Like a Sith]]'', an article featured in the [[Star Wars Insider 134|''Star Wars Insider'' 134]].<ref name="SLS" /> Sith is the second working conlang ever developed for the ''Star Wars'' universe, the first being [[Karen Traviss]]' [[Mando'a/Legends|Mando'a]].<ref name="MPC">{{InsiderCite|86|The Mandalorians: People and Culture}}</ref>

While Grossblatt's system is realistic and functional, there are conflicts between his version of the Sith phonology and Sith vocabulary established in previous works. While the ''Star Wars Insider'' article states that the Sith has no 'e' 'p' or 'f' sounds, words or names such as "derriphan" "[[Ffon Althe|Ffon]]," "aleph", [[Jen'ari]], [[Jen'jidai]], [[Jensaarai/Legends|Jensaarai]] or "[[Ludo Kressh|Kressh]]" have appeared in older canon sources. Not even "Korriban", the name of the Sith species' homeworld, can be written using this system, due to the lack of 'b'. In fact, even some of the new words that were invented for ''Book of Sith''&mdash;including "Grotthu" and "Zuguruk"&mdash;cannot be properly transcribed.<ref name="TBoS" /><ref name="SLS" /> Although Grossblatt did create "new" Sith words consistent with his conlang for the caste names, they did not make it into the final version of the book.<ref name="Grossblatt e-mail" />
